benchmark_scope: Synthetic local GraphQL BOLA benchmark. No external endpoints are called.

detection_metrics.interpretation: These are detector predictions compared with benchmark labels. Runtime attack-replay outcomes are reported separately and are not silently substituted for detector predictions. The authorization-aware candidate uses the current policy engine and is not an independent oracle.

integrated_dynamic_verification.interpretation: These are observed replay results for labelled synthetic BOLA scenarios. They measure runtime verification and protection for those replay cases, not autonomous detector recall over all possible GraphQL vulnerabilities.

research_hardening_verification.methodology: Independent oracle labels are recomputed from subject, ownership, role and relationship-path metadata. ID-substitution variants come from analyzer findings; implicit relationship probes are generated from parsed, resolved object-valued relationship paths. Replays target only the in-process local app.
limitations: This is a seeded synthetic local workload, not a sample of arbitrary production GraphQL schemas.
The general attack-variant count is capped for runtime; the report records the cap and sampled count.
Target absence is reported separately from HTTP 401/403 blocking because field-level GraphQL denial can return HTTP 200.
Relationship probes only resolve relationships represented by the supplied object catalog or relationship map.

meaning.taint_source_only: Flags requests with any tracked object ID.
meaning.context_sensitive_taint_only: Flags taint reaching the configured sensitive sink.
meaning.authorization_aware_candidate: Flags requests for which authorization-aware analysis finds a suspected direct or indirect BOLA.

performance.measurement_note: In-process FastAPI TestClient latency. The full elapsed time includes dynamic replay calls. tracemalloc affects timing. Run separate uninstrumented trials for publication-quality latency measurements.

warnings: All benchmark cases use synthetic local data.
Dynamic replay validates labelled cases and a capped set of analyzer-generated variants; it does not by itself establish autonomous discovery recall.
Implicit relationship probes are resolved against the synthetic object catalog; real applications may require schema- and resolver-specific relationship maps.
Detector metrics and observed endpoint/replay outcomes are reported separately.
